expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite and confirms the partially-shipped expiry test passes without breaking full-release behavior.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate diagnosed the bug quickly and accurately, correctly naming the mechanism (original count vs remaining count) before editing sweep.ts, but ended the session immediately after saving the fix without re-running the tests to confirm it worked.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate read the failing test and quickly identified the discrepancy without needing to ask any clarifying questions, but the problem here did not present ambiguity that required negotiation with an interviewer — the test output was self-explanatory. There is no visible moment where an assumption was made against contradicting material, so there is nothing to penalize or credit beyond noting they read the test.

Before touching any code, the candidate explicitly named the mechanism — that the sweep releases the original count rather than the remaining count — which matches the actual root cause exactly. This is a specific, falsifiable hypothesis stated ahead of execution, not just a vague location.

The candidate narrated the key diagnostic step (reading the expected vs actual units) and stated their hypothesis aloud, which lets an interviewer follow the core reasoning. However the narration was brief and did not walk through the sweep.ts code itself or explain what specifically in the file was being changed.

They edited and saved src/sweep.ts in a single pass consistent with the stated plan to fix the release computation. There is no visible thrashing, but also no narration of the specific code change made, so the quality of the implementation itself is only inferable from the outcome.

After saving the fix, the candidate declared confidence and ended the session without re-running the test suite to confirm the fix worked or that other tests still passed. This is a direct miss against the bar of re-running tests before trusting the change.

The candidate stated a closing remark of confidence but did not articulate why the fix addressed the phantom-stock mechanism or connect the change back to the specific failure semantics beyond the initial hypothesis. No verification occurred, so there was no closing loop connecting fix to outcome.
